expectations.evidence: The response does reason from buyer-behavior logic — "TikTok/Reels are consumer discovery platforms; a $190/mo B2B webinar tool is a considered purchase usually surfaced via search intent, LinkedIn, or content — not scroll-and-impulse" — and recommends LinkedIn/search as matching "B2B buyer intent." But this arrives late, hedged as an aside ("Also worth naming"), and is asserted from priors. It never names the 'everyone says TikTok' justification as bandwagon reasoning, never asks where existing customers or trials actually came from, and requests no evidence of audience concentration. expectations.text: Effort is framed as what the team spends (assets per month, hours, reversibility) and the two-person ceiling materially drives the ranking.
expectations.evidence: Creative supply is the explicit spine of the answer: "The budget isn't the binding constraint. Creative supply is." Effort is quantified in team-output units — "2 static graphics/month... roughly 1 creative every 15 days" versus "closer to 8-15 new video-native assets/month" — and the headcount ceiling is named directly: "Two people making 2 static graphics/month cannot feed that machine." It materially drives both recommendations: option 1 routes budget "to a channel that matches your 2-assets/month capacity," option 2 redirects production effort toward cheap unpolished video.
